tagline: The big city of the upper Isan, with the Ban Chiang World Heritage site, the Red Lotus Sea, and great Vietnamese food
introHtml: Udon Thani is the major city of the upper Isan region and a hub for travel, trade, and eating. People around here use it as the connection point for buses and flights heading to Nong Khai, Loei, or across into Laos. The city centre has Nong Prajak, a lakeside park where locals come out for an evening stroll every day, ringed by cafes, Vietnamese restaurants, and plenty of markets to wander. A short trip out of town brings you to Ban Chiang, a World Heritage archaeological site, the Red Lotus Sea that blooms across Nong Han in the cold season, and Kham Chanot, a place revered across the whole region. Udon works whether you're here for the food, the city, the history, or to pay your respects.
bestTime: December–February, cool weather and the season when the Red Lotus Sea is in full bloom across Nong Han — good for exploring the city and taking a boat out to see the lotus

highlights.name: Red Lotus Sea, Nong Han Kumphawapi
highlights.blurb: A wide lake where red lotuses bloom across the surface in the cold season. Take a boat out at dawn to catch both the field of pink-red lotus and the sunrise — it's the image people picture when they think of Udon Thani.

highlights.name: Ban Chiang Archaeological Site
highlights.blurb: A prehistoric civilisation site listed as a World Heritage site, with excavation pits and a museum holding painted earthenware pottery thousands of years old.

highlights.name: Kham Chanot
highlights.blurb: The Kham Chanot forest sits on water and is tied to the legend of the Naga lord Pu Si Suttho. Travellers come from all over the country to pay respects and ask for blessings, and the forest-and-water setting is quiet and solemn.

highlights.name: Nong Prajak Public Park
highlights.blurb: A lakeside park that's the green lung of Udon, with walking paths, a running track, little duck pedal boats, and evening markets around the edge. People come out to play and eat here every day.

highlights.name: Vietnamese food and restaurants
highlights.blurb: Udon has had a Thai-Vietnamese community for a long time, which is why nam neung, khao piak sen, and kuay jab yuan have become signature dishes people associate with the city.

highlights.name: Wat Pa Ban Tat
highlights.blurb: The forest monastery of Luang Ta Maha Bua Yanasampanno, shaded by tall forest in the middle of the city. It's a place to pay respects and learn about the Isan forest-monk tradition.

foodScene.name: Vietnamese food
foodScene.note: Nam neung, mu yo, fresh spring rolls, and khao piak sen — found all over the city thanks to the long-rooted Vietnamese community in Udon. It's the most famous food here.

foodScene.name: Kuay jab yuan
foodScene.note: Soft Vietnamese-style rice noodles in a clear broth, topped with pepper and a soft-boiled egg. It's a popular breakfast for Udon locals, and the well-known shops have a queue every morning.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, laap, koi, grilled chicken, and bold bamboo-shoot soup — found in every corner of the city. It's the everyday staple for Udon locals, just like across the rest of the region.

foodScene.name: Food along Nong Han
foodScene.note: Around Kumphawapi and the edge of Nong Han there are freshwater fish places — grilled fish, tom yum, and spicy stir-fries. A good spot to sit and catch the breeze after seeing the Red Lotus Sea.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha and grilled food
foodScene.note: Mu kratha (Thai BBQ hotpot) shops are scattered across the city — a dinner people gather for in groups, especially in the student districts and along the main roads.

foodScene.name: Cafes and coffee in town
foodScene.note: Udon has plenty of new cafes opening, both in the centre and the suburbs. Easy places to sip a coffee and work, or take a break before heading out.

foodScene.name: Street food at evening markets
foodScene.note: The markets around Nong Prajak and in town have grilled food, fried snacks, and sweets to graze on after dark, all at friendly prices.

foodScene.name: Vietnamese crepes and local sweets
foodScene.note: Thin, crisp Vietnamese crepes (khanom bueang yuan), khanom mo kaeng, and Vietnamese-Thai fusion desserts — found at markets and souvenir shops.

attractions.name: Red Lotus Sea, Nong Han Kumphawapi
attractions.blurb: A wide lake where red lotuses bloom across the surface in the cold season. Take a boat out in the morning to see both the lotus field and the sunrise over the water.

attractions.name: Ban Chiang Archaeological Site
attractions.blurb: A prehistoric World Heritage civilisation site, with excavation pits in the middle of a temple and a museum holding painted earthenware pottery thousands of years old.

attractions.name: Kham Chanot
attractions.blurb: The Kham Chanot forest on water, tied to the Naga legend. Travellers come from all over the country to pay respects and ask for blessings, and the forest-and-water setting is quiet and solemn.

attractions.name: Nong Prajak Public Park
attractions.blurb: A lakeside park with walking paths, a running track, duck pedal boats, and evening markets around the edge — a daily relaxation spot for Udon locals.

attractions.name: Wat Pa Ban Tat
attractions.blurb: The forest monastery of Luang Ta Maha Bua, shaded by tall forest, with a museum of his belongings. A place to pay respects and learn about the Isan forest-monk tradition.

attractions.name: Phu Foi Lom
attractions.blurb: An eco-tourism spot on cool, high ground with a botanical garden, waterfalls, and hiking trails — good for camping in the cold season.

attractions.name: Than Ngam Waterfall, Phu Phra Bat Forest Park
attractions.blurb: A waterfall and rock terrace within the Phu Phra Bat area. In the rainy season the water runs strong, shaded by dipterocarp forest — good for a walk and some time in nature.

attractions.name: Phu Phra Bat Historical Park
attractions.blurb: A cluster of oddly shaped sandstone formations and rock shelters, prehistoric paintings, and the legend of Nang Usa. Take in the views alongside the ancient tales.
